title: Cathan's Journal [Castle]
text: Just waiting for Spitfoot to bring me the keys, then next stop is the blue-flamed door in the swamps. It holds the secret to Velgar’s destruction, I just know it. For now I’ll bide my time, enjoying the spectacle of goblin hospitality.  I enjoy being a goblin’s prisoner, there’s a kind of dance to the whole thing. They threaten, they shout, they exclaim all the horrible things they intend to do to you, and then they never go through with it.  Goblin culture is like that. The strong hold power, but it’s mostly performative -- because if you make yourself too much of a threat, someone’s gonna challenge you to make you prove you deserve it.  The dragon hasn’t learned that lesson about goblin faith.  Bandos was a nutjob, Zanik will tell you, but he got his people to behave exactly how he wanted. Conflict for conflict’s sake, everyone just itching to beat up their boss. Which is how I’ve got a few of them wrapped round my finger – because I’ve let it slip that I’m gunning for their god.  Velgar isn’t a god, he’s just a dragon, but he’s the toughest guy around and so they treat him as such. But I’ve worked out that path to taking him down and enough of these guys are thinking that I can do what I say. So they’re coming with me, we’re making a coup, and big old green-and-scaley’s getting an axe to the face.  Just as soon as Spitfoot gets here, we’ll make for that blue-flamed swamp door, where there’s a piece of the puzzle that’ll set my plan in motion.

title: Cathan's note
text: Old Vannaka’s an odd chap. Loyal to a fault, but not one to show affection. I still remember how he trained me, instilling me with a hatred for him that pushed me right past the pain. He was merciless, he was relentless, his training made me ache every day. So I took months of resentment and I balled them into a fist and with all of my loathing rammed it right into his face.   He was so proud. So proud that I punched him. So pleased with me for bruising his jaw. Because that was the first time I had walked on my new leg, without having to think through every painful motion. He had given me something else to turn my loathing on, that wasn’t myself. That lummox took a broken kid, ready to give up on the world, and turned him into a warrior. He’s a good man, Vannaka, even if he won’t always admit it. So of course, I said I’d join him on this new adventure. I feel like there’s more than just a curiosity here for him. Something deeper. Something hidden. A pain behind the eyes. So, yeah, I’ll help him find what he’s looking for. It’s what a good friend does.

title: Cathan's Journal [Ghornfell]
text: The goblins warn me about Ghornfell and the creatures within it. They call them the garou, and they shiver when they say it. I’ve heard them mention them before, in the stories, myths and legends of this place – beastial warriors, that Bandos came here to destroy. He failed.  The god of war, failed to destroy the Garou and their goddess. That should tell you something.  I’ll be careful. I’ll sneak past their fortifications, I need to get through to the tower that rises in the heard of these Fractured Plains. That’s where Velgar rests.  That’s where I’ll destroy him.

title: Ritual Of Purification
text: Our Kings, who have ruled at the highest peak for generations, each carry a single piece of home with them. From the old home where our ancestors came from, there is a single pebble in the token that the king wears about their neck. Over time and exposure to this land, that pebble becomes corrupted and tainted by this place.  But corruption can be purged. Rot can be cut away.  Seek the altar that sits where a heart once beat. Pillars of bone reaching for the sky, longing to touch the moon in memory of the lost one. There, her power echoes still, able to wash away the stain of this world.  Place ram horns, two of them, as an image of the goddess so that her power has a vessel to work the miracle. Anoint then the token with the oil of the lapis vine, crushing three of the bulbs over the token. Storm and oil, anathema to the corruption.  Offer a prayer in memory of her. Lougrim, the Huntress in moonlight, is gone but not forgotten. Do this and a piece of home shall be once again restored. Such is the way of our kings who rule on high, closest to the sky and the memory of her silvered radiance.

title: Laboratory Note
text: I wonder, sometimes, whether we are too limited in our focus. Is the cold-blooded nature of the reptile, more useful than the mammalian warm-blood approach? I watch the creatures of this region, the kebbits, the cows, the sheep and I see how they multiply and spread at a pace that far exceeds our own. By contrast, the dragons I birth are a slow and laborious effort. Each one must be carefully managed and maintained with focused precision. Even those capable of spawning their own young, do so slowly. Often brooding no more than a single viable progeny in a century of practice. Even my prize specimen produced only a single heir, a red-scaled whelp, no less, unlike his mother’s multicoloured hues. Perhaps the fault lies in the father. I should dissect him and see where the problem begins. But I lose my train of thought. Mammals - Noisy, smelly, but they are everywhere, breeding like rats – which are also mammals, now I think about it. Perhaps I should turn my sights on them instead. There are a pack of dire wolves that wander near my laboratory, it would be simple enough to procure a few of their number. Some adults, a few children, I’ll need a large and diverse sample size for my experiments. Perhaps there’s a place where reptile and mammal can meet, to create a superior creature. I shall investigate further.

title: Experiment Log
text: Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 7 It is not easy splicing reptile and mammal together, their very nature fights against their biology and they would rather perish upon emergence than live with such a hybrid nature. It’s a shame really, the little pups are quite cute. I think Viika would like one as a pet, it might keep my sibling grounded and anchored a little more to our frame of reference. Wishful thinking perhaps. The wolves have proved remarkably durable, considering. While they all die seconds after birth, they do hold on longer than expected. I attempted to combine kebbit and dragon and… well… that didn’t go well. Chinchompa and dragon, that was a mistake that will take some time to repair – I liked that lab.  Yet wolf, there’s something here, I can feel it. They’re resilient, dangerous and there’s something in the pack mentality that fascinates me. Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 56 I have decided that a rapid hybridisation approach will not work. Mammals, while fast breeders, are weak and lack the resilience needed to survive the experiment if I go too quickly. Instead I shall engineer a slow breeding process, spreading the development out over the generations. Tedious, yes, but at least it will allow me to focus on other project while this progresses. Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 219 The changes are gradual, yet viable. Scales here and there, some improved musculature and reflexes, yet nothing approaching the power of a dragon. Is this all they can be? Dragon-Hybridisation Experiment Day 2307 I’d forgotten about this failure of an experiment. The dragon-wolves have proved inadequate for any useful purpose. I was going to incinerate the remaining members, but Viika in a fit of strangeness released them all. So, now we have it. Dragon-wolves running all over the region, lovely. Honestly my sibling can be so vexing sometimes.

title: The Tale of the Ghost Wolves
text: There once was a girl with a pet she adored. He had fur like silver, eyes like ice. The gentlest of natures. He was ever so nice. But there were things in the forest, Full of shadow and hate. When the girl found her friend, It was sadly too late. Eyes like glass. Skin cold as stone. The girl wept for days. She’d never felt more alone. Smoke rose through the woods, Clawing and thick. When the girl breathed it in, It made her feel sick. Yet in the choking and coughing, There whispered a voice Beautiful and terrible, And it gave her a choice. She could live as she was, Alone in the night-black, Or make a pact with the smoke, And get her friend back. She didn’t wait for a second. She agreed with glee. So the smoke told her to wait. Where her best friend could see. Eyes like embers. Fur like fog. Her last words uttered. “You’re a very bad dog.”

title: Dust-covered Diary
text: 17 Novtumber 4207 I miss the monastery, with its moss-covered walls and the chill breeze that spreads to your bones. They don't have that here. The Ashenfall breeze is strong and cold, but it seeps into your bones and causes shakes, not shivers. It's the sort of cold that acts as a warning. I think this whole continent is out to get us. I just wanted to preach the blessed teachings of Saradomin in the warm comfort of a nice church made of stone not wood. I miss the city, with it’s bustle, noise and smell. The crisp country air is too sterile for me. Still, I'm here to save the souls of the lost. In this age of constant conflict, it's nice to find a small village that just needs a sermon or two.  We shall bring into the light of Saradomin's truth. They seem eager, abandoned as they are by their pagan patron, but they're still mired in their old ways, and it'll take time to drag them out. In time, maybe we can turn this mud-filled little town into a new heart of the Saradominist faith- something with the right kind of smell.

title: Bloodstained Journal
text: 31 Raktuber 4213 As I write this, the villagers die around me. I cower beneath broken timber, hoping they do not hear the scratching of my quill against the page. I use my own blood as ink, like some infernal contract, but no matter how much I write prayers for salvation, no one hears my plea. It was the beasts, the garou, who came for us, and they were not alone. I had thought them eradicated. The alliance with the war god and his foul-smelling minions, was so we could wipe out their moon goddess and cleanse the forests of their filth. We were so assured of our victory and we were so close to success. But now, now their moon goddess rides atop a scaled nightmare. Flames for breath and swords for fangs. Beside her came two creatures I had never seen before. Scaled, winged, wicked, like the great beast the goddess rode. Around one was a halo of fire and the other was rimed with frost, scribbling a tally of our deaths in its journal. They burned the city to the ground. Murdered the lord and his knights. We scattered into the woods, doomed. Saradomin, where are you?

title: Priest's Journal
text: 4 Bennath 4210 I sometimes find my thoughts wandering to home. I’ve been here for years, yet my heart will never belong here. It’s odd to long for a war-torn realm, a world where armies are on constant move and the threat of death greets you with a familiar smile each morning, like a bosom companion. That’s home. War - A war raging for thousands of years. A war between the very gods themselves, a scale of destruction that must have been unthinkable before. Yet this is the only life I have known. We’ve brought some of that war with us, of course. The high priest and the local lord have brokered an alliance of swords with Bandos’ goblins. Horrible little creatures, who want nothing but the thrill of slaughter. There is a shared enemy between us and we’ve agreed to wipe them out. The garou,  and their blasphemous goddess, they’ve overstayed their welcome. We were here first, and we’ve no desire to share. Bandos wants revenge, for some slight or other the goddess created. We want to regain what is rightfully ours. So we’ll work together, and we’ll wipe those monsters out. There can be no peace with animals.

title: Scrawled Diary Page
text: I don't remember the date, Fentuary maybe? 4265 I know there’s no real reason to write this. No one’s going to read it. It’ll rot to nothing in time, even with the druid’s and their silly little rites. I think I’m just writing in this journal, because I want to take these memories out of my head and put them somewhere else. If I do that, maybe, just maybe, I can have one night’s sleep without hearing the screams. The village is gone. Velgar, a great dragon, green as the grass, killed everyone who lived there. Nothing left but cinders and screaming spectres. There was peace for a while, with the garou and their dragon army. We called a truce and the garou accepted, as long as we each kept to ourselves. For decades it held, and we almost forgot about battle, until we felt the ripple on the wind as a goddess died. That’s when we knew that a new war was coming. No, not a war. This was a massacre; we never stood a chance. Kuldra’s forces unleashed hate wreathed flames, and entire settlements vanished overnight. Goblin, human, gone in an instant. Perhaps we deserved it.

title: Tear-stained journal
text: A cold, dark day in the year 4267 of the third age,  I am lost, and yet he does not look for me. I wait, oh, how I wait for you, oh Saradomin. I have been your faithful servant, and yet, here and now, where are you when I need you the most?  They’re dead. All of them. Everyone is gone. I hid beneath the rubble, trying to ignore the stench of their rotting bodies as I hid from the beasts. So much death, so much pain, and still, he does not come to save me.  Have I sinned? Have I committed some hateful act that has offended you, oh great Saradomin? Is there any act of contrition that will save me from this endless nightmare? No - No, you were never that sort of god, were you? Only ever your glory, not ours. We’re nothing to you, are we? Just pawns in your games? Well, I refuse to play any longer. I spit on your name. I curse your countenance. I cry out into the dark that someone makes you suffer like you have left us to suffer.  Why did I ever think you could save us? Curse you, Saradomin.

title: Grimey Parchment
text: Haha, I am writing on this paper thing, like a human. I am funny. Other goblins laugh.  This place is place for adventurers and heroes. Big shiny armour and swords that aren’t as rusted as they should be. Silly humans used to come here and pat each other on the back for not being eaten by a monster today. Then they would be sad when eaten by a monster tomorrow.  They all stupid.  Best way to not be eaten by a monster, is to not be near a monster’s mouth. You run in the other direction, or you gang up on the monster with lots and lots of friends. If someone eaten, better chances it not you if there are lots of you.  See, goblins smart. Humans stupid.  Writing stupid too. What is point of words on page, when words could be said out loud?  Humans say pen mightier than sword, but I don’t think it would parry mine very well.  Maybe it’s magic? I should test. I will ask Mucktooth to fight me with it. I bet he die.   He died.  Pen is rubbish. Sword much better.

title: Grubby Note
text: 23 Raktuber 4163 Guthix forgive me, but I hate goblins. They’ve recently found their way to Ashenfall, and immediately started causing trouble. They’re strange little creatures. Green skin, powerful arms and an odour fouler than anything I’ve ever encountered. They seem to delight in nothing more than picking a fight with anything that moves. Or sometimes doesn’t move, I’ve seen them do battle with a rock. Mostly I ignore them. They’ve tried to raid my hut a few times, but never in large numbers. I give them a sound thrashing with my broom and that’s normally enough to send them packing. They’re a pain more than anything, hardly a threat. The threat is their god. I never met Guthix, I’m far too young, but I hear stories of how he towered above everyone and his presence made the air feel heavy. Their "big high war god" feels the same. Huge, hulking and layered in metal. A more brutal creature I dare not hope to meet. I dread the day that he decides to turn his ire on us, but thankfully his attention is focused elsewhere, on the beastmen of the wilds. Good, let him focus on them.

title: Weathered Diary
text: 13 Wintumber 4209 It’s cold this time of year, though not as cold as the legends say. Perhaps Ashenfall’s climate is warm and pleasant. Maybe the magic of this place keeps the winter at bay? There was a snowfall, heavy and solid, that trapped me in this place. I warmed myself by the fire and another joined me. The goblin, Globfinger and he’s more pleasant than his name suggests. He came in out of the cold and in the spirit of our people’s alliance, I shared a warm meal with him. We spoke of battles, as goblins always do. I wonder if they know of any other activity other than conflict, yet if they do, they dare not speak of it. We regailed one another with tales of fights against the wildfolk, as goblin and human cut down the beasts. Goblins may be uncouth, undisciplined and smelly, but they celebrate well. We laughed with one another and cheered on our clans. He told me he is glad that his god had beef to settle with the moon-goddess, otherwise we would not have had such an enjoyable war. He’s right. I have enjoyed a righteous cause. Perhaps, goblins aren’t so bad.

title: Pungent Scribble
text: That weren’t meant to happen. It were meant to be lots of us and lots of the humans, and then we were meant to skewer the beastmen on the end of our spears. Big high war god was gonna be real pleased with us all, and then we were gonna have a feast. Instead we’re the feast! That’s not fair. That’s not how it meant to work. There I was, chasing down a beastman runt, when a great walloping dragon comes outa nowhere and lands on the goblin boss man. Squashes him into jelly, and not the good kind with bits of fruit – the bad kind, with bits of chieftain. Then, dragon goes for the rest of us, breathes a great big jet of fire which turns all of me friends into charcoal. When did dragons work with beastmen? Why did dragons work with beastmen? What did dragons? Huh? Thinking make my head hurt. Sod this, I’m gonna go hide in a cave til it all goes away. Goblins good at hiding in caves. Probably nothing bad in caves.

title: Muddy Scrawl
text: Big high war god has left us. Big high war god ran away. But you can’t run away, that illegal. Big high war god said so. What do we do when big high war god say one thing, then big high war god do another? I ask priest, priest said he a baker now – not a very good one, he burns the bread. All priests very confused and argue over answer. We decide that since dragon won against the big high war god, then dragon must be stronger than big high war god. Which means now we worship dragon, because that’s how faith works. Religion very confusing, can see why priest become a baker even if priest can’t bake. Going to workship dragon now, maybe he make us dragons too? I bet goblin dragons would be strongest dragons of all. Velgar is new big high war god. Glory be to Velgar. I hope new god isn’t hungry.

title: Preserved Diary
text: Today, I summoned a miracle. Thanks to these new stones, gifts from the great Guthix himself, I have performed a spell warding wood from rot. My hut, simple as it is, will now stand the test of time for generations to come. Even this journal and these silly words on paper will stand unsullied for aeons to pass. That such wonders are so commonplace is truly a miracle.  Glory be to Guthix.    He calls these stones “Runes”. Within each of them is an element imprisoned and waiting to be unleashed. The more complex the combination of runes, the more intricate the spell, and the more we learn about them, the more fantastic our workings.  Overnight, our world has changed. We no longer use flint for fire when a snap of our fingers serves the same effect. The air can be used as a blade that makes wheat harvests easy. It is the dawn of a miraculous new era where we can make a better world.  This new continent must be so full of wonders if it has led our lord to create these marvels.

title: Druid's Memoirs
text: I walk beside Guthix as we explore this strange land. We arrived on familiar green grass that echoed our homes, yet the more we explored, the stranger it became. There is an oddness to this continent, a sort of curse that changes things the deeper they get toward the centre.  There are wolves with manes made of leaves and deer with reed-like fronds as natural a part of them as their antlers.  Trees, with leaves of shifted hues that emulate the sunset. Grass the colour of candlelight.  It’s as if Ashenfall takes something and twists it, infusing it with magic. Not destroying it, not even harming it, but making it different. Perhaps, in time, that might happen to us. I think I would suit a beard made of leaves.  Guthix is fascinated, too, as much as a god can be. I see a smile on his face as he walks through the woods. It is as if he has discovered the beginning threads of a secret, and he seeks to unravel the knots.  I look forward to the revelations to come.

title: Soot-stained Diary
text: Even gods make mistakes, though his bring him laughter. Even as the lab explodes, Guthix’s latest experiment brings him almost child-like joy.  We pick ourselves up from the rubble and are met by mischievous giggles. There is a whimsiness in him that is usually crushed by a hidden melancholy, but now the mirth is on full display.  All over a rock. A piece of stone that he found hovering in the air as if it found gravity disdainful. He was fascinated immediately, sensing in it a potential our mortal gaze could not see.  Over the months, he has poured into the stone what energies he can gather. Guthix believes that the elements themselves can be tamed within the rock.  We knew he was serious when he brought the great stone with him. Power radiates from it, and there’s a pressure to it like it’s the wall of a dam, and it’s about ready to burst. But it worked, and Guthix laughed with glee when he bound the very air itself into the rock.  He gave it to me, and I cast my first spell. A miracle in the palm of my hand. Glory to Guthix.

title: Ancient Journal Page
text: We are lost without him, though we pretend otherwise. The absence of his divine presence is felt through every household. We pray, follow the rituals, and live our lives as best we can, but it is not the same.  Was he right to be angry? Lives were lost after all. So many dead, far too many, and we justified it because we told ourselves that they were no longer human. They were Amalgamated. They were impure, imperfect -- wrong.  Our hatred must have been like poison to him. To see this tranquil home we had created fall to bitter infighting and needless hate. For there is nothing so human as to despise.  He left. Took some of the faithful with him, those who had not fallen to our cruel prejudices. In his last moments, he tasked the Wild Knights to uphold their oaths, protecting both us from the wild and the wild from us, and then he left.  The captain of the Knights took some of the abandoned children under her wing. Those whose parents were lost to our venom. It will be a hard life, but better than they’ll have here.  We are such fools.

title: Forgotten Diary
text: We have fallen so far as to go from god to godless. Worse still, to have the vile beastmen parade their own deity in front of us as though we’re unworthy of divine consideration.  She is beautiful and alien like all such beings are. Her words are soft and gentle, though the barbs are barely hidden. Her presence is a statement that any harm to her people will be met with swift retribution, and we lack the power to stand up to a god.  We’ve managed without Guthix’s presence for centuries now. It should be easy. Yet, when I see her moonlit figure glide through our village as she and the chieftain meet for diplomatic conversation, I can’t help the envy that stirs in my gut. A green-eyed worm writhing in jealousy.  We were abandoned. They were not. Aren’t we more deserving than the beasts? I pray that we are found worthy again. That a god reaches their gaze toward us and recognizes what we’ve created. Ashenfall deserves to be a human nation.  I refuse to let it fall to animals.

title: Servant's Secret Diary
text: No one in the castle knows what I am. They barely know who I am. I walk these walls as a shadow, forgotten and unseen by all who dwell within. Priests, nobles, and gurning knights, none of them know that I am a Child of Darkness, a servant of shadows within the Duke’s court. I could bring death. I could bring chaos. I could bring pain to them all. With a few carefully chosen words, or some redistributed wealth, it would be oh so simple for me to bring these Saradominist fools to their knees. I wash their socks. I bring their meals. I spit in their mugs before bringing them breakfast. All that while I stand beside them as the architect of their future downfall. There’s another meeting of the Children of Shadows soon. Apparently, there are rumours of secret structures, buried under the ground and the other Children believe that they might contain something we could use to remake this sad, pathetic world. A weapon, perhaps. New magic to wield. Some dread, and deadly monster we could unleash upon these fools. So, yes, my Duke, I’ll bring you your socks, and your drinks, and your scones. But mark my word, I’ll bring you your end soon enough. Hail Zamorak!

title: Duke's Diary
text: The priests are very helpful, always offering advice, always steering me in the right direction. I was wavering over how to handle the old Guthixian followers, you know, those weird people in the leaf covered rags, and the priests gave me the most helpful advice. Just send them away. So simple really, why didn’t I think of it. After all, those druids so love the forests, the woods and those weird, damp, little caves, that they’d be delighted at the chance to go and move into them. No longer frustrated by the noise of progress, they could return to their quiet contemplations about squirrels and twigs. I assume that’s what they do. The priests are so wise. I mean they must be to put my family in charge of this place. We were once simple officials, but now look at us, the Dukes of Brynmoor. Noble rulers of all, just as we deserve to be. They’re coming over to talk with me later, something to do with our little Garou problem. I’m sure they will have most delightful solution to the situation. I would very much like to expand our little kingdom into Ghornfel. Pink is my favourite colour, after all.

title: Torn Journal Page
text: Raktuber 1466 They came in the night. The driver fell first; his life quickly ended with an arrow to the neck. Eva grabbed her staff and prepared to unleash a torrent of flame on our attackers, but a crack of thunder sent us sprawling across the forest floor.  Eric vanished, yelping as something dragged him into the tree line. Only for the scream to silence suddenly with terrifying finality. I readied my bow as Eva hurled flames into the woods and, in the flickering lights as her fire blast dwindled, I caught sight of yellow eyes glinting in the darkness. Pure evil. They charged, sweeping out of the forests like shadows with teeth.  Like wolves that walk on two legs, almost human in their stance, but in the short-lived embers of Eva’s magic, I saw no sign of humanity – only malice. They ran at us with saliva dripping from elongated fangs and claws that glinted unpleasantly in the moonlight.  I felled two of them with my arrows before they caught up to Eva and turned the evening’s rain a horrible shade of scarlet.  I ran, and they let me escape.  They’re toying with me.  I can’t run far enough.

title: Garou Writings
text: I do not understand this concept of hate. The god of the greenskins feels it toward us with such a ferocity that you would think he was preparing for the hunt. I could respect that, but it isn’t his way.  Instead of chasing us down or challenging our strongest, he sits in fortified battlements and sends an unending river of green-skinned warriors to smash against our defences. Even the smallest pup has slain a dozen of the vermin, yet their numbers seem almost endless, and there are always more to kill.  This relentless assault continues through the day and the night. As we rest, their sacrifice continues. As we tire, they gain ground. When we sleep, they push forward. We are losing this war, and it is not because of strength.  I asked the goddess why they do this. What honour is there in such a shameful display? She says it is because he is jealous of us. Enraged by some slight we inflicted, some aeons ago, on a world far from here.  He hates with such fury that he would see his own people slaughtered just to wound us. A single drop of our blood, for oceans of theirs.

title: Scorched Journal
text: Ire Of Phyrrys 4213 The beastman and their goddess no longer stand alone. Our alliance forced them back into the shadows, and we were so close to removing their stain from this sacred land. Yet, somehow, they have plucked new friends from the shadows. Allies of a terrible power that we had no inkling of before.  The dragons they summon are terror enough. Setting fire to our villages, burning our watchtowers to ash. This would be dangerous enough, yet the four commanders scare me the most.  They are smaller than the dragons but bear their features. Great leathery wings and glistening scales. They wield frightening magic that decimates battalions, and they do so with the cold impartiality of the rat catcher.  In their eyes, we are nothing but vermin, and they treat us appropriately.  Not all are killed; some are taken. Dragged into great vaults filled with nothing but screams. I hear rumours of cruel experiments and sick entertainment. Yet most of us are nought but food for their beasts.  Is this some malicious form of justice? Were we wrong to betray the beastmen when we did? Saradomin save us. Nothing else will.

title: Leathery Parchment
text: My people have a tradition that is sacred above all others; the right of challenge. There is nothing we respect more than strength or cunning. When one defeats a challenger, they prove themselves rightful of their position. When one fails, they prove themselves inadequate.  Even gods must acknowledge this truth.  The High Queen, lady Lougrim, earned her place by challenging the kings of old. Taking on all of them in one mythical battle and emerging the victor. In the centuries that have followed, she has held her position and bested all challengers that think themselves her rival.  That winning streak ended today when the dragon queen took the throne.  The battle was swift and bloody; their clashing energies created cracks in the very earth. The entire continent buckled beneath their fury, but only one of them could prevail. Her many heads tore the goddess limb from limb, swallowing down the pieces of her divine flesh until nothing of the old queen remained.  Now we have a new queen, and long may she reign.  Hail to High Queen Kuldra, the god eater.

title: Elder's Storybook Page
text: Before your grandfather had teeth, there was a king who was stronger than all his rivals. King Rolthar was mighty, proud and gifted with cunning. Moon after moon, challengers would throw themselves at him, and each fell before the hour passed. He was beloved by his citizens, a wise king who kept our people strong. Yet his strength was so great that none could match him, and it birthed a melancholy he could not escape. He sought foes that might prove a challenge. Seeking a victory worthy of praise. He chose to face the dragon. Velgar was the strongest warrior in the realm. Rolthar spent months in preparation, crafted a blade of iron and sounded the challenge horn. The dragon was too strong, his scales too solid, yet the king refused to relent. When Rolthar’s strength finally faltered, and his last breath escaped, he still held his blade. Velgar slew Rolthar, as all strongest must, and brought the body home. “This warrior is the pride of your people,” he told the tribe, “give him a burial worthy of his strength.” His resting place now sits high on the mountain, watching over us. Remember King Rolthar, little pups, for the worthy must never be forgotten.

title: Dragonkin Journal Page
text: I have never understood my brethren’s calling to cower in the safety of dreams and let reality slip away. They choose to sleep, to pretend that our suffering does not exist.  Pathetic.  While they tremble like hatchlings in the cold, I look to the future. This continent could be home to a kingdom. A new start, a new Orthen. One not chained down by the weakness and arrogance of our elders.   The first, great, Dragonkin empire? The stone here is sturdy; magical energies imbue it with a strength unlike any other on this pitiful planet. They can be tamed and shaped, even made to defy gravity itself. The magic Rasthin showed us is more than just power; it’s understanding. I listen to the stone, and I know how to shape it. It’s as simple as reaching down and telling it how it should be.  Now, thanks to the aggressive natures of the lesser races, I have a workforce. The beastmen are stupid and easily distracted, but they are strong and know how to work. They are excellent tools, and I shall use them to craft a monument worthy of the name Brakka.

title: Dragonkin Diary Page
text: We are finally free from our kin’s grasp. They can no longer hunt us down, searching for Lacrussa’s accursed sibling. To know the future and yet not offer us guidance, what is the point of a seer that does not see?  Rasthin urges patience, Avisk calls for calm, and Lacrussa ignores us, content to have her family returned to her. All of us stand in defiance of our kin’s traditions. We forged our own path and found somewhere new.  This continent is remarkable. It is flush with energy that seeps into the stone, the trees, the water, and even the air, and it feels alive with possibility. The creatures here are transformed, taking on aspects both elemental and primal. What wonderful possibilities this place offers.  I can do a lot with this continent. The stone looks sturdy, the metal firm. Even the wood feels as though I could make it last centuries before it rots into nothing. It is the perfect place to create a new home. To fashion the foundations of the next dragonkin city.  Viika whispers that the structures will last. Dragonkin towers standing against the flow of time.   Monuments to my genius.

title: Infused Journal
text: We used to talk about power as if it were some ephemeral notion—a collection of things—status, skill, charisma, all stacked together in one umbrella term. But that’s not real power; this is. What now courses through my veins is the embodiment of that word. In me is the very essence of the stone itself.  Not just the stone but the earth, the dirt, and the plants that grow within it. I feel each of them, and with a wave of my hand, I make them follow my will.  Is this what it feels like to be a god? To command dominion over elemental earth? It moves as I beckon; it shapes as I command. With a thought, I conjure a tower that would have taken me months to craft before.  Kerapac was a fool to seek the Anathema. The real power is here, in this place. The discarded afterthoughts of the Elder God’s dinner, but in our hands, it’s a magic without equal.  And they do not stir in response. They slumber still, ignoring our ascension.  Viika was right. This place is special. Yet they choose not to claim the gift. Why? I wonder.

title: Dragonkin Notebook Page
text: I despise the rambling of seers. Viika persists with their inscrutable announcements of something sinister to come yet lacks the ability to make their meaning clear. Lacrussa fusses over their sibling as they have their little meltdown while irritating me with their lack of clarity.  Precision is important. Vagueness helps no one and causes more harm than good. Seers never understood this. I remember speaking to Kranon once, long before his fall, and he laughed with me about the eccentricities of the timeswept. He explained how they exist in moments of their lives other than the ones we are bound to, lost in eddies of temporal currents while the rest of us are anchored in place.  It seems like a cruel existence, to be certain, but that does not make up for the frustration they create.  What do they mean when they say, “the blood makes her hunger”? What does that even mean? Who are these “warriors from across the sea” that will “put an end to her vengeance”. Who is “her”? Who are they? What in creation is the seer talking about? Enough - I’m done. I leave Lacrussa to her sibling’s nonsense. I have more pressing things to do.

title: Bloodstained Page
text: My wound is a lethal one, so I leave this message as a last letter to my siblings in arms.  I am proud to be one of the Wild Knights, chosen by Guthix to defend people from nature and nature from people. I am a guardian between two worlds, and it fills me with pride. But what I encountered just a few days prior was not from either world.  It was a monster. A demon. Blade-like talons where arms should be, and it arrived in a flash of purple lightning. Its chitinous hide repelled my blade, and my spells caused no sign of flinching. I found it in the fog as I wandered that poisonous swamp searching for a fugitive. I found the criminal; just as his bloodied torso slipped into that wicked maw.  The universe has its own sense of justice.  If it hadn’t fed, I am sure I wouldn’t be here. It was sated, slower than it could have been, giving me a chance. Barely - It plunged one of those wicked pincers through my stomach, and I narrowly escaped with my life.  What’s left of it.  I pray my siblings do not find it.

title: Leaf-scented Page
text: We Wild Knights rarely gather. We spend so much time alone, wandering the wildlands, that we can go weeks, sometimes months, before speaking to another person. This can stunt our conversation, or sometimes the inverse.  Aidan is the talkative kind. He turns solitude into a gaseous buildup that he belches upon each of us as an endless stream of words. Every thought, feeling, and tiny observation is unleashed upon the rest of us the moment we meet.  But today, there is silence, and I find I miss the noise.  Aidan died valiantly defending his brothers. A group of them went out in search of some beast—some foul, fetid creature in the poisonous fog. It’s clear that they found it and that it led to his death. His brothers mourn him silently; they’re alive because he isn’t.  I think he would prefer to be mourned in sound.  Lamented with cacophony, a wake of jeering shouts, one night of endless chitchat in memory of him. A brother lost, a brother remembered. Two left who’ll carry his name, as is tradition.  He died to save them, so they now proudly bear his name.

title: Vault Hunter's Journal
text: I've been searching for weeks and yet still I've found nothing. My notes have led me here, to a secret hidden within these ruins, and this statue must be the key.    The goblins make investigation difficult and I am running out of arrows, but I know there's something here.    Previous reports suggest there's an ancient vault nearby. A dragonkin structure full of secrets. Perhaps it might go someway to explain this symbol scratched across this statue's plaque. If I can find the entrance and make my way past its defences, perhaps I can find the answers I seek.    There are so few of us left now, fate owes us this one.

title: Ravanna's First Journal
text: The odd thing about life is it’s surprisingly easy to maintain. For all the work of alchemists and scheming sorcerers, continued existence is child’s play really. All it takes is hate. Hate is a fuel that can burn forever. Pure rage is a force that can drive anyone forward. Grief is a power source that can last until the end of time. You just need to know how to use them. There’s a morality in vengeance that society shuns. They say it won’t solve anything. That it never makes things better. Yet, I picture the suffering of those monsters and that’s all I need. Knowing they suffer, die and weep for their loved ones, that’s enough to drive my bones forward and keep the skin stitched in place. Unreasonable, yes, but at least hate is honest in it’s hypocrisy. I choose to turn the wheel of the vicious cycle round and round, grinding garou bones beneath it. I will never forgive them for the death of my friend. Never - And as long as I curse them, my soul will not fade to the world below. Someone will tell me that that’s not what Ulv would want, but I knew my friend and, if he could speak, he’d tell me to make sure they hurt. So, I do. Those same people tell me that grief fades, but that’s a lie. It’s been so long now, so many years, yet that pain and that hate still burn inside me more ferociously than the sun, and I wake each day smiling because I know they suffer in return. Perhaps I need a hobby?

title: Ravanna's Second Journal
text: So this is what the people who left Bramblemead are up to. Honestly, it seems like a pretty nice life. There’s amalgamated and, for lack of a better word, normal people working side by side. Shops are well-stocked, and fields are filled with delicious looking vegetables. The entire landscape is a dazzling display of vibrant colours and … oh, yeah, they have dragons. Not dragons like we had – the ones that burn villages to the ground and stomp on people for fun. No, these dragons watch over the villagers, help them with construction, farming, all sorts of stuff. They even give them this weird little thing they call a Blessing, which somehow binds them together in a way I’m seriously going to need to study later. The people don’t worship the dragons either. There’s nothing like the goblin shenanigans down south. No, the traditional religions line up in a multifaith community with one another. Saradominists greet Zamorakians and no one starts a fight. I assume, anyway, no one really wears little badges or anything, but there are shrines to more than just Saradomin here, so I like to daydream. I set up a little shop. Can you imagine? Me, with a shop! Just selling little potions and salves, and services for those that need to speak with the dead. Simple stuff, nothing too taxing, but enough to put a roof over my head. I think I could be happy here. Well, as happy as I get.

title: Ravanna's Third Journal
text: I have a new customer, and she won’t fit through the door. Odd to empathise with a dragon, but I do. We all saw what happened. I watched as the great multi-headed dragon queen pulled Xikotal’s heart from his chest and ate it in front of his mate. You don’t just get over something like that. It’s visceral and cuts you deeper than you ever thought possible. It’s not just grief. It’s not just rage. The two forces combine into something new, something stronger than the sum of its components. That sort of feeling is powerful – strong enough to change you into something other than what you were. I have lived for longer than I can say on that feeling alone. It’s a fuel that rages within you, burning you from the inside to keep you warm. I can only imagine what it’s doing to a creature like her. She asks me to bring her beloved back, but that’s beyond my power, always has been. I’ve never been great at animating the dead, I can do a few bones, sure, but nothing stronger. Curses, though, that I’m good with those. Imaru’s rage makes her the perfect focus. The beating heart around the darkest magics. She can be a weapon against the Godeater, if I hone her right. The rage of a dragon, combined with the power of a grief-curse, such a thing could be the blade needed to slit Kuldra’s throat. I will forge her carefully.

title: Ravanna's Fourth Journal
text: I am guilty of mistakes, I admit this. I let things get to me and I don’t think them through as well as I should. When I lost Ulv I tried to bring him back and… well… the result of that is better buried, I confess. I visit him from time to time. There’s nothing left of my friend there, hasn’t been for some time, but I don’t want him getting lonely. She was my next mistake. Imaru - After the death of her mate she came to me seeking a way to bring him back. Necromancy doesn’t work like that, at least not yet and certainly not within my skill set. Yet, still, I thought I could offer her something almost as good. I offered her revenge. I created a curse within her, using her grief and rage as a focus, so that it might strengthen her against Kuldra. She was to become a devouring force that would feast on the Godeater’s very soul. It did not work. Kuldra is stronger than I imagined. Her essence more powerful than either of us could have guessed. As Imaru raged at her Kuldra simply laughed and rebuffed her, barely even registering the unholy force hurled against her. She is a monster, and I use that word very rarely. So Imaru died. Fell to the ground in a crumbled heap… and I wish that were the end of it.

title: Ravanna's Fifth Journal
text: Things are so much worse than I thought. The River Noumenon, the way to the Afterlife, is blocked. Imaru has somehow wedged herself in there, using the curse I gave her and her own, sheer, bloody-minded rage to stick her in place. She claws at the edge of the Underworld, creating rifts that bleed the Noumenon’s waters into our world like some deadly poison that rips out the soul. She uses her “Blessing” as an anchor to her people, dragging their souls to her so that she might feast and grow stronger. So focused on strength and power, on beating Kuldra, that she doesn’t think about what happens to everyone else. My soul is protected, warded by the curse that rages inside me, but the other villagers aren’t so lucky. I see tendrils of their spirits being dragged from their chests like a ragged cloak billowing in the wind. They don’t see it, of course, but they can feel it. They know something is going on and it’s leading to blind panic. The once peaceful chatter of Fellhollow is now turning to stifled screams. This is all my fault. I need to try and find a way to fix it.

title: Ravanna's Sixth Journal
text: Fellhollow is doomed, there’s no other word for it. Imaru’s wedged herself in this part of the underworld and her mouth is wide and consuming all the souls that flow down the river Noumenon. With each soul she devours she grows stronger and her grip tightens. Her hunger grows, she craves more and more, and she’ll never stop. The necromantic energies of the Underworld then wash back through the Blessing and into her subjects, animating their bodies and filling them with an unquenchable thirst for more souls. They’re nothing but withered husks of themselves, all humanity drained away and all that’s left is a terrible, clawing, need. I’ve seen this before, in the forbidden texts that my master kept hidden from me. Only the source of this evil isn’t some nebulous power that dwells in the shadows, but an undead dragon. An evil of my own making. So, one I must undo. I cannot break the curse. I cannot end her wrath. For all my skills I am nowhere near a match for her in battle.  All I can do is protect the rest of Ashenfall, and Gielinor, by keeping her locked away. It’ll take some work, but the one thing I have in abundance is time.

title: Ravanna's Seventh Journal
text: The seals are in place, but I’m not sure what good they’ll do. A desperate attempt to try and mitigate some of the damage I’ve caused by binding Imaru to that curse. I have taken the essence of her curse and bound it to the plinths, in hope that someone stronger than me might yet claim them. Doing so will bind them to her curse in the same way that she is, but only for a while. Strong enough to challenge her. Strong enough to harm her. Without the curse she’s invulnerable, but the very same thing that makes her powerful, makes her weak. I have split them across the region, so that someone will not stumble on them by mistake. It will require dedication, focus and skill to overcome this monster of my own making, I’m sorry I cannot be the one to do it. But, at least, I can help the one who can.

title: Lacrussa's Journal
text: Viika is silent today and I don’t know if that’s a good sign. How do you relate to your sibling when they’re seeing a different “now” to you? Are they staring back at the door to our home as our parents wave them goodbye forever? Or are they enjoying tomorrow’s dinner today instead? I wish they could tell me. Share how they feel. The scientist in me would give anything to know the mind of the timeswept. The sister in me would give anything to understand my sibling. Dragonkin don’t normally do family. We’re all so focused on our own problems, our constant pain, that we sometimes lack the empathy to care for someone else. Romance died the day of the curse, I swear, and family became a necessary act of survival, rather than a nurturing thing. Yet I choose to defy traditional values. Viika deserves better, after all. So if they do not know what day is today, I will keep them grounded. I will be the shield against the horrors of the present, so that they will see the tomorrow they’ve already lived. And perhaps, if I’m lucky, they will find that special moment when their now and my now coincide together.

title: Lacrussa's Notes
text: Dragons are a useful tool, but little more than that. They are powerful, yes, strong and dangerous, excellent beasts of burden or disposable troops in a fight. Yet, they lack the grace, poise and power needed to be new dragonkin hosts. I always knew that was a failed plan. Still, what experiment cannot be perfected? What hypothesis cannot be refined? There is something in dragons, some key to our apotheosis, that I feel driven to explore further still. And Rasthin has the blood that may be the key. “Gods”, they call them, what a nonsense affair. Leave that to the waning priest caste, like that mewling fool Kranon, and the primitive spirits these lesser beings follow. They are powerful creatures, formed of a changed and ascended essence, as if flesh and soul merged into a single construct and solidified into form. One of them bleeds. Perhaps all of them, but this one for certain. She calls herself a goddess of the moon and the primordial hunt. Nonsense, of course, moons are rocks floating in the emptiness and there’s nothing spiritual or metaphysical about a predator seeking lunch. Still, if I can refine this power? If I can merge it with a dragon, perhaps… just perhaps… I can turn these worthless dragons into something we can use.

title: Lacrussa's Ravings
text: Avisk is like the scales behind my wings, irritating and in desperate needs of a good scratch. He keeps coming to me and trying to explain to me how I need to do X with the dragons, or Y with their eggs, as if he, an Aughra, has the slightest understanding of real science. Imbecile - His obsession with crystals is growing increasingly tiresome.  He’s already messed with some of the brood, tried to use that strange rune essence in ways that would cause energy to flow in certain ways. I can see the concept he’s going for, but his clumsy nonsense just leads it to ruin. Trying to create some sort of enhanced mind for the dragons, as if they could exist like a swarm.  All of them, of course, died. All but one, and she’s turned out strangely. I encourage the growth of a single head for the dragons, keeps them sane and stable. There’s no good that can come from multiple brains in charge of one body, yet she proves me wrong. All the minds work as if connected, as if part of the same whole. A single consciousness spread across all of them. A single personality. Because that’s what it is, a personality. A will. A mind of her own. She is enraged, yes, like all dragons are, but she spreads it across herself, weakening the effect. I have encountered curiosity, reason, even wit. A most curious creature, I look forward to studying her more.

title: Lacrussa's Writings
text: There is a crack in the heart of the world and it whispers. Smoke rises from it unlike any I’ve encountered before. There is no magma vent. No burning coal line underground. There is just emptiness softly smoking, chill as the grave. Smoke should be warm, yet this is colder than ice. A sort of strange frost that seeps into your bones. Though it strangles the air in my lungs as I stare into this fissure, I see only darkness and shadow, all the way down. There is a power in it, unlike any I’ve seen before and I must harness it. It started with the claw-bones of one of the failed dragon whelps. Exposed to the smoke it twitched and writhed, as if there were still muscles and sinew contracting in motion, not polished bone with no nerves attached. There is a song in the whispering smoke. Discordant and strange. Words I don’t understand, I’m not even sure it’s language. Still, I feel a connection there, like a promise, offering me more. I am not fool enough to listen, the angler fish lure of power is all too familiar to my kind, but still perhaps I can make use of this. After all, one must risk everything in the pursuit of knowledge!

title: Lacrussa's Diary
text: Avisk is a snake! I am not surprised by this discovery, he’s never been subtle about his ambition, but that he would dare to attempt an experiment on Viika, well that’s unforgivable. He attached tubes, crystals and all sorts of nonsense to my sibling’s head and attempted something with rune essence that caused a lot of explosions. Viika was hurt, burned across their temple and one of their wings is damaged enough that they might never fly again. I have never felt anger like I did in that moment. Even the rage from the curse never struck me as hard. In that instant I dragged blades of ice from the aether, and I would have torn Avisk to pieces of only my sibling hadn’t said “no”. Always too gentle Viika, not like the rest of us. Maybe that’s why they never partook Rasthin’s discovery. Because they knew what monsters we’d become. Avisk won’t get away without consequences. My sibling may be gentle, but I am not. I flow like the river and wield the patience of glaciers, and Avisk will learn that water always wins.

title: Mould-covered Journal
text: I fled, like the coward I am, back toward Bramblemead, back to the hatred. Yet, the way is closed. A great wall bars my path. I am a prisoner here among the damned. We all tried so hard to stem the tide. The Wild Knights to the east pushed back against the horde as much as they could. They walled themselves away in their keep  until no one remains alive to guard it. Emberwood sealed itself away behind a barrier, priests working together in unified cause. Faith locks everyone out, and everyone in. As for the tower, and those who dwelled beside it, it’s shattered. The dragons’ disciples lost in a great lake of sorrow and grief. Damned by their own devotion. And here I am, clawing at a wall, mere metres of stone between safety and despair. Despair always wins. Perhaps it is like those doors? I see them sometimes, out of the corner of my eye. Strange and ephemeral, inviting me in. Yet, if I focus on them, I see nothing. Only when I feel myself slipping away do they show themselves again. Perhaps a wall is not always a wall, like a door is not always there? It doesn’t matter. I am lost. Fellhollow is lost. It’s all her fault.

title: Withered Journal
text: Death leaves its mark on the world. You feel it around graveyards, mausoleums and on the remnants of ancient battlefields that claimed hundreds of lives. It’s a pressure that presses against the air and weighs you down. Here the air is crushing, I feel myself being dragged to the floor by the grief and the rage attached to these bones. Xikotal, Imaru’s mate, lies here dead and gone. His soul long since passed to the Afterlife, leaving Imaru alone and angry. Perhaps he was lucky to pass before seeing his mate like this. See the monster she has become since her death. Still, this grief makes a powerful fetter. A thread of connection strong enough to forge a seal. I’ll lay it here, in this vault, protected from the dead by the dragonkin guardians. Hopefully that will keep it safe enough that no one can set this dread dragon free.

title: Soot-stained Journal
text: I found an egg today, buried in the earth. Looks like it fell out of one of them there ruins, you know, the ones under the ground with the glowy blue flames? Well there was this egg that was just sticking out of this weird little pot and so I took it, you know? Thought it might make a good omelette or something. Scarius says that I’m being stupid, but he just wants to omelette for himself. … OK, so, right, omelette is a no go. Tried to crack the egg, no dice. Smashed it with a hammer. Still nothing. Sword? No chance. So I figured it might make a nice ornament or something, keep the barracks nice and decorative like. … Egg hatched today. Coincidentally, on the same day I lost two of my fingers. I get it though, poor thing was hungry, can’t begrudge a baby the occasional nip. Little green thing, scales and all, reckon it’s a dragon. Seems like a nice one though. Captain wants me to kill it, but I’m not gonna do that. Poor thing just needs some love and some steak from the kitchen and they’ll be a good little beastie. Need a name for them. Maybe Fang because they’ve got enough of them. … Captain acting strange today. Came back from the town all shaking and weird, says there’s some sort of infection or other, people going weird. I’m sure it’s nothing to worry about, I’ll just focus on keeping Fang well hidden. Don’t want anyone to know what I’ve done.

title: Red-stained Diary
text: There are strange visitors to these lands, people I never expected. Unsettling, pale elves who arrive in the night and stay for an evening asking us very unusual questions. I don’t even know why we let them in. It was as if they belonged here… as if they had a right to be here. We spoke of travel and family, of loss and of love. They asked me about the scar on my lip and the way I hold my sword at an angle. I told them about my first crush, even though I’d never shared his name with anyone. Then there was the talk of loss. Loss, like it was happening right then. A bottle spinning, fingers pointing, a choice we never chose to make. We lost someone that night, didn’t we? I don’t remember who, but there’s a hole there where a person should be. A shadow over my memories. A locked room, where no one has the key. I remember laughter, dancing and eyes like perfect rubies sparkling in the dazzling night. I remember his lips on mine, cold and tasting of metal, and then… nothing. Their names. I don’t remember those elven names. You’d think you’d remember something like that. It’s not like we see many elves, not since that bard passed through a while ago. I feel like I should know them. But, like all those empty rooms, somehow, I forget.

title: Priestly Journal
text: Scripture says that all gods other than Saradomin are false, and their cultists are not to be trusted. Yet, I don’t see it that way today. As the village has fallen to the shambling nightmare that is the withering, the other priests and I have worked together to save who we can. There are dead buried deep below the soil and their bones carry the power of prayer in them, like all do. So we priests prayed together, a union of faith, to erect a barrier of belief to keep the withered villagers contained. Our prayers bound to the icons, and only together will the village be re-opened once more. A tragic loss, truly. Emberwood could have been the great human utopia. Faiths working side by side. Amalgamated and not – villagers who do not let their differences define them. Two great dragons, to watch over us and keep us safe. It could have been perfect. But belief needs adversity, or it becomes complacency. This will be a trial for each of us that we must strive to overcome.

title: Weathered Diary
text: It is a strange thing to leave one’s home. All those old comforts, those familiar sights, smells and memories, just left behind. Stranger still, is leaving because you just don’t recognise it anymore. Were we always so cruel? So callous and so shortsighted that we turn on our own just because they’re a little bit strange? So Jenna has seaweed for hair and eyes of literal sapphire. Isn’t that something to love about her, rather than hate? Home is changed now. Those familiar sights are stained in horrid crimson. Those sentimental scents are tainted with a worrying touch of iron. Memories incinerated by rising flames, burning hope just as old neighbours burn away the homes of everyone different. So we leave. We go north. Past the garou who snarl even though we have a treaty, and then down into the deep dark of the earth in search of a new home. One we pray will stand longer than the last. A home we can be proud of.

title: Lazilly-penned Diary
text: You’d think they’d be cruel landlords, given that they’re dragons and all. After them beast people turned on our Southern neighbours and wiped them all out, you’d expect these dragons to do the same. They was working together after all. But, no, that’s not how it goes. Or at least not how it’s going. The two of them kept their distance at first, pretending we weren’t here. We watched as the flight of dragons swept over us and ignored us altogether, fearing the side eyes from our two new friends. Then, when it were all over and done with, here they were. Talking to us, as though we were neighbours. Speaking to us as though we were friends. She were… kind. There’s no other word for it. Great big blue thing made of teeth and claws, and she were singing to the children who couldn’t sleep at night. He and her, helped us build this city. Helped us find the best places to fetch water, or plant crops. Her magic brought rain and his calmed the winds, so that our harvests were plentiful, and our population bloomed. All it costs is a few sheep or cows, every once in a while, a pretty good deal if you ask me. No gods watching over us here. No priests, nor nobles. We got dragons watching out for us, aint that a nice thing?

title: Dragon-embossed Journal
text: I have seen what love looks like, and it spirals through the clouds. Serpentine patterns entwined together as they dance in the sun’s rays and share the sky with one another. For such large creatures, you would think them incapable of grace, yet I have never seen a dance so beautiful as the two of them together. My grandmother speaks of their dance with a smile on her wrinkled lips. Telling stories of how the villagers danced the same, hand in hand, around the dark fires of winter. Bringing love and hope and joy in a musical war against the dark. Yet, there is a knowing sort of sadness when I ask where the dragons' children are. Because I have never seen them. Perhaps that’s why they are so kind to us. So gentle. Why they crush the bandits as they ransack our villages, or why they toss the dragon wolves out into the cold. Because we are their children, in a strange sort of way. Gran says that’s what the Blessing is, that little dragon magic in our bones. An enchantment woven over each of us, as part of the dance. It makes us healthier, makes us heartier, makes us better than before. I can’t wait to learn a dance of my own. Perhaps I can spiral through the clouds like they do, wouldn’t that be a wonderful thing?

title: Battered Diary
text: He’s dead, the black-scaled guardian. As he died it was as if the wind stilled in mourning, a great silence spread across the land dragging away all motion and noise. Leaves stopped, as if frozen in the moment. Clouds halted staring down at it all in horror. Everything was silent… except for her sorrow. The lament of a dragon is primal, perhaps even primordial. Our lizard-brains bow their heads in mournful empathy for her suffering. It is as if a wave of misery crashes against all of us, drenching us to our bones in grief. The writhing heads of Queen Kuldra, the Godeater, laughs from the sky. Her echoing mockery felt by every living creature in Fellhollow, as if we’re all a joke to her. A passing diversion, before she destroys us all. She doesn’t, because that would be kind. She does not end Imaru’s pain, not yet. She leaves her with the agony of loss and the dissolution of her dreams for the future. A cruel punishment, for the simple crime of peace. She dared to shelter the lost and wandering humans, rather than put us to the flame. Empathy, her only sin, and for that she must endure a loss so deep we may never understand it. How do you survive eternities together, ripped away in an instant?

title: Weathered Journal
text: I have heard about the God Wars, in the stories that Grandfather gives. He passed them down from his father and his father before that, tales of epic battles and destructive forces beyond reason. This must have been what clashes between gods felt like. Imaru and Kuldra, raging against one another using Ashenfall as a weapon. The wind became knives, the rocks hurled as cannon-fire, and the rain turned to hail, falling like great-hammers on everyone caught in their path. Cataclysmic powers crash against one another and each blow feels like it might tear the continent apart. She feels different this time, Imaru. Changed - Like her grief and her rage have been forged into weapons and she slams them against the Godeater with unbridled hate. In response, Kuldra laughs, even though her armour shudders against the force of it, scales falling to the earth like the beginning flakes of winter snow. There is a sensation in my chest -- strength being leeched from within me as Imaru presses the attack. I see old Mrs. Mossfoot stumble, hand across her chest, as each of the other villagers feel it too. The Blessing, a source of strength, now feels like a hole in each of us, draining us dry. But for Imaru we’ll endure it. Against Kuldra we’ll stand. Fellhollow does not fall this day!

title: Withered Diary
text: I am still here. I am still here. I am still me. I am still me. I am withering and I cannot hold it back. It begins with silence behind the eyes, as if there’s nothing there but the most basic of needs – the need to feed. More and more of us, ever since Imaru’s defeat and death at Kuldra’s claws, feels part of ourselves slipping away. I am dragged outside my being, I am drawn beyond my skull, my skin, myself. And the world changes the more I am pulled away. I see things that were not there before. Flickers, out of the corner of my eye. Doors that were not doors before. I see a great river undulating and flowing but rising and flooding as though something is blocked within it and forcing it to overflow. But the worst is that feeling, of eyes upon me. As if something is not just watching me but focused on me. A predator waiting to strike. I’ve seen what happens to those consumed by it. They walk still, but there is no life there, only hunger. A need to grab, claw and rend the living, desperate for a piece of the soul that seems lost. In my bones I feel a tug, a current, drawing the part of me that’s… me… away. I don’t want to become one of those monsters. I am still here. I am still here. I am still me. I am still me.

title: Lacrussa's Memoir
text: Avisk keeps trying to sneak into my laboratory, convinced that the secrets within will grant him the knowledge to transcend his mortal frame. I’ve told him time and time again that it will do no such thing, but he’s convinced I conceal my discoveries, hoarding knowledge and sharing it with none. Have my advances not brought this little group to the heights of success? It was my work that allowed Rasthin to complete her device. My work that created armies of dragons to serve at our beck and call. Yet, despite all this, he’s convinced that I keep the really good stuff to myself. The irritating part is, of course, that he is correct. So, I seal it away behind locked doors shielded from even dragonkin magic. A mechanism that will stand for eternity, barring him access. The best part is that I based the lock not on a key, which he could steal, nor on a phrase, which he could overhear, but upon a riddle posed to me by the priest Kranon, all those years ago. “What does the charitable priest offer, the illuminated sage seek, and the ignorant forsake? Walk their paths and what do you discover?” He will go mad knowing the answer, for it is obvious, yet it is the steps one must walk to get there that will unbar his path. I bet he’ll even think the damaged statue is accidental wear and tear. It will drive him mad. Just thinking about his frustration makes me giddy with delight.

title: Rot-covered Journal
text: I am lost in these treacherous ruins, with all hope of the outside world lost to me. I sought to escape the horror of Fellhollow, but this place is worse. Rotting from within.  Yet, as I wither… as these bonds of flesh are broken, another world reveals itself.  Walkways, doorways, entire new paths to travel. This prison is filled with ways to run that were not there before.  Still, as I explore them, I feel her gaze upon me. I feel her hunger grow. Imaru is watching, and there is no escape.  Saradomin have mercy, because Imaru most certainly will not.

title: Farmer Fred's Journal
text: I had always wanted neighbours, out here in the sticks, but these weren’t exactly what I imagined. Refugees, so they claim, from the Bandosian forces, escaped the violence of their people in hope of peace. Followers of the war god, looking to settle down. I didn’t believe it, until they turned in their weapons. There was this great pile of them outside the village, built up into a pyre and then set to the flame. We danced as they burned, it was beautiful. I drank with a few of them and… well… I don’t remember much of the evening anymore. Just hazy moments of laughter and stories, nothing more than that. Now I bring Golbor and Klom baskets of pumpkins and in exchange they help me plough the fields before we can sow the soil anew. Good people. Full of laughter and big emotions so large they create a gravity that draws all of us in. These weren’t the neighbours I imagined, but I couldn’t ask for better.

title: Ulgo's Diary
text: Duneday Ulgo made friends with man in the woods. Could not see face but they were very friendly. Made lots of pretty noises at Ulgo, though Ulgo does not know their words. Tomorrow Ulgo is going to go and see if they want to play catch with him. Papa says that everyone loves playing catch, even though the villagers need to stand very far away so that the ball does not hurt them. Threw stone once, because had no ball, and villager wouldn’t talk to me again after. Ulgo very sad. Villager never spoken to Ulgo again, so Ulgo cannot even say sorry. Twiblick Ulgo’s friend was in the woods again. Got a better look at him, his skin was all shiny and special. Maybe he got paints? Ulgo will ask Papa if he can get paints. Friend in wood played very rough. When Ulgo threw him the ball, he did not throw it back. Instead he ran at Ulgo and tried to wrestle. Ulgo only ten, but Ulgo very strong, Papa always says so, and Ulgo push friend away. Fun game. Laughed a lot. Even though new friend bit me a few times. Must have gotten overexcited. Ulgo understand, Ulgo bite too. Ivanday Ulgo hungry. Feel slow and strange. Need to eat more. Maybe Mama make Ulgo something. Duneday Ulgo hungry. Papa’s arm taste bad. Notduneday Ulgo hungry. Day Ulgo hungry.

title: Captain Rainer's Journal
text: Of all the horrors of the rising dead, none are quite so chilling as the enormous undead ogres that now roam the lands. While all the vile undead seem filled with a hunger they can never sate, these beasts have a hunger greater than any other, and a terrifying capacity to consume. Some of the scouts first saw them near the village borders, trying to break through the barricades to gain entry. Ogres are terrifying at the best of times, even the peaceful refugees who settled here, and these are scarier still. It’s like gazing up at a wall made of muscle, that wants, more than anything, to eat you alive. There is no malice behind their eyes. No cruelty. There is just emptiness and hunger and the understanding that you might be lunch. What scares me most about these creatures, is that their undead nature defies the theories we’d been working under. Since it was the villagers who first began to change, we assumed that it must be something to do with the strange magic their dragon patron worked upon them. Since most of us had not undergone this so-called “Blessing”, we thought we were safe from this terrifying transformation. Yet, these… zogres… throw that theory out the window. They received no blessing, so how can that be the source? And if they can be affected, then surely so can we? Perhaps that would explain why I’m getting hungrier, no matter how much I eat. If that’s the case… then we’re all doomed. Fellhollow will fall.

title: Scarecrow's Scribbles #1
text: No crows, Place to doze, Sun on m' toes. Bliss - Where was I last? Did I lose something there? I have a memory of...digging?

title: Scarecrow's Scribbles #2
text: My memory is fading. Was I someone else before? My mind is so foggy. Or was it just foggy in the place I left? A name comes to me. Joe?

title: Scarecrow's Scribbles #3
text: I don't have much time left. Soon, I will forget everything. All I can do is choose a place to be. I have so many regrets. But I suppose they will leave me too. Joe -

title: Scarecrow's Scribbles #4
text: How could I have known she was a witch? I stole the seeds to feed myself, to make something from this scrap of land. Now I am cursed. Cursed to become something that no-one will look twice at. Even now, I can feel my mind failing me. the best I can do is find a fine spot. There, I suppose, I will live out the rest of my days. Joe -

title: Nolan Scathe's Journal
text: We have plundered the very depths of Fellhollow and perhaps we have dug too deep? What lays buried should stay buried. Each of us turned from the other, back to back and walked away. Not one of us alone knows the location, only together will the secret be revealed.  And we are no longer talking.

title: Eleanor Scathe's Diary
text: I have chosen here to rest, to close my eyes and never see the dawn. I am tired, so tired, and will welcome the longest, deepest sleep. I hope my companions found rest in their final moments. Between us all, we will keep the secret.

title: Samuel Malcifer's Journal
text: A bunch of backstabbers, each of them, cowards and fools. The wounds we gave to one another guaranteeing no one will ever find our treasures. A shared plunder, between us all it lays buried deep.

title: Winston Henning's Diary
text: I wonder if we shouldn't have left it buried. If we should have brought it back to the village for all to see. What wonders, what secrets, could we reveal? Answers to questions we never knew we had.  Now, between the four of us, that secret lays buried. I wonder if that is our greatest mistake?

title: Badly Scrawled Note
text: Do not go to Dowdun Reach, traveller. Turn back now while you can. Even if you are faithful to the Dark Lord - no, especially if you are faithful - do not risk the madness within these walls, lest it condemn you and your faith to ruin. We had thought it nonsense that the mages here would delve into the darker magics. They were charlatans. Harmless magicians. They were meant to pull rabbits from hats and flowers from their sleeves. Instead, they have learned more sinister arts, older and more wicked than anything we could imagine. Saradomin has cursed them, I am sure of it. A malady suitable for their blasphemy. They seem consumed with madness, with hatred; a bestial rage that burns away all sense or reason. Do not go to Dowdun Reach, traveller. Only horror awaits you there.
