title: Alric's Plan (Part 1)
text: The thought came to me as I slept. Should I worry that my genius rises when I am defenceless? Rasmodel would do much with that information. You see, nothing enthralls a demon more than other demons. They despise and bicker, drawn into a game of spite.  It may seem like repulsion, but in truth they are drawn to one another. They live - should you call it living - to be in each other's company. Knowing this to be true, I think on my skills of possession. I am still mastering the art, but there have been breakthroughs. I am able to siphon a soul from the living and store it in the inanimate, just for a moment. My goblet gained the soul of a slave (and filled with tears! A delightful discovery). My mirror reflected only my last, sycophantic apprentice, for a time, at least. If I could bottle and transpose the soul of a demon - or whatever makeshift thing they have as a soul - could I infuse a demonic gateway? My theory, my hope, is that the gateway would enthrall others of their kind. They would be drawn, consciously or subconsciously, in numbers that we could barely contain. A portal like that would need an incredible number of demonic souls to keep powered, but, in that respect, I am not worried. The infernal gate would supply itself.

title: Alric’s Plan (Part 2)
text: If I were to weigh Rasmodel, he would have one ounce of value. That ounce is his leadership, or, more specifically, what I have learned from it.  He has taught me that when you make a mistake, you do not run from it. Instead, you claim it was your intention all along. If a scouting party is killed, they were traitors that you sent on a suicide mission. If the sewers flood and illness spreads, you were building the troops' immunity. Admit nothing, own everything. My infernal gateway is no longer a gateway. The tens of thousands of demon souls are no longer powering it. It seems that they have been quietly bleeding into the fortress itself. Each brick now whispers with the avernic. They are in the walls. Demons now summon themselves, at their own whims, from any room. I do not run from this. It was my intention. I claim it. This is what I tell my magi: there is no corner of Dowdun Reach that is safe from us now. If you connive against us magi, a demon may be listening. If you walk without a partner, an avernic may digest you. This is the rule of the keep now.  All that remains is to find the voice beneath the voices. I know it is there - I can hear it. Once it is identified, I will claim it, too.

title: A New Pestilence
text: Can't focus in my quarters. There's three of us in there. Too crowded. I can string thoughts together here. Not many - a few gems on a necklace. We are afflicted by not one, but two diseases. They tussle, fighting. A cure needs to kill them both.  I thought, maybe, if I poison one - the weaker one - then the other will eat it. Wither - Die -  I think I know where the weak one resides. I hear it whisper in my left ear. I will dropper the toxin there. Let it feed. Yum - Let the toxin spread. Shush! The chicken and the master come again. I must look busy. Busy busy busy busy busy.

title: An Acolyte's Guide to Demon Handling
text: I'm out of here - being transferred to the Library. These are my handover notes. Don't worry, you'll get the hang of demon-handling in no time. 1. 'Demon-handling' is a turn of phrase. Avoid touching 'em. 2. Marrentil round the nostrils helps with the sulphur smell. 3. Demons don't like it if you copy their gruff voices. 4. While they may not cover up their nethers, you would be wise not to stare. 5. Awfunctious has learned to copy Alric's voice. Alric'll only talk to you if he wants a cup of tea. 6. Alric likes white tea, no sugar.  7. Always look at what you're signing. Requisition forms have a habit of being swapped for demon pacts. 8. You can tell it's a demon pact because it reeks of sulphur - even the marrentil won't stop it. 9. When locking up, make sure to test your binding spells. Festilius has a habit of finding flaws and unwinding them.  10. If you lose Festilius, he'll be in the chicken coop.

title: Goblins of da Reach Unite!
text: Frends of da rebel lotion, it is time to drop da shackles of Lord Rasmo-smell and All-thick. Dey promised us gold an food and travel back home, to da Felldips. But have dey provided? NO - Dey have not provided. We only have food scraps which WE have to cooks! I call on us all to rise up, like bread. Sneeze at da means of production! Stir snot in da soup. Cough gunge on da bedcovas. Take arms against da oh-pressers! Their pressing time is OVA! We meet in da shed near da waterfall at sunny down time.

title: A Report on the Withering
text: Lord Alric, please find the group's assessment of the necroseismic event that the locals call 'The Withering'. The people of Fellhollow are not well-equipped for the contamination. They have grown soft through their freedoms, and have mostly resorted to panic. We are the only ones studying and measuring the effects. It is our belief that the subcontinent of Fellhollow will be entirely contaminated in the next two weeks. It spreads at a significant rate, roughly a hectare a day, and is only slowed or halted by mountains and bodies of water. By our calculations, the size and breadth of the Dowdun Mountains should protect us. We would like to emphasise 'should' here: there is a risk that waterways and crevices in the rock may lead to intrusions. We mean intrusions in the broadest sense: the effects of the Withering, necromantic incursions and unwanted refugees. It is our recommendation that all efforts are made to seal Dowdun Reach. We should be focused on removing these opportunities for intrusion. All connecting pathways to the subcontinent of Fellhollow should be severed. We should also post knights to the crypt. It will be our canary in the mineshaft. If the dead rise there, we will know that the Withering has breached.

title: Hall of Heroes
text: Dowdun Reach isn’t just the home of warriors. It is the birthplace of legends. Those who refused to follow the limited, vapid doctrines of the Saradominist faith and come to understand that freedom itself is a virtue worth fighting for. Within these halls rest the pathbuilders and wayfinders for a new world order. One born of personal choice and freedom, rather than tyranny and oppression. They are not interred in nearby graves, nor scattered as ashes across the firmament. No, they rest within these very walls, each statue housing what is left of their earthly forms. There is Isla, known as the Blood Witch, or the Lady of Screams. She was the first to prise the secrets of runecrafting from the blue robes wizards, passing that knowledge on to our own mages so that we might tear open the veil of reality and make bargains with the infernal realm. Gregor Volrath, the Mountain Lion, defended these mountains in the days before the keep was tall enough to defend itself. The mithril lines crags were too tempting for the neighbouring villagers and Gregor held them back with hammer and shield. Each statue houses a legacy. Each stone stores a soul. Each footstep that echoes through these walls, is a reminder of the great heroes that walked here before.

title: Archmage’s Note to Students
text: Apprentice - a word, if you will. I see that you are eager to progress. That's good. Eagerness will get you far under the gaze of Zamorak. Eagerness needs two partners, however. Power and knowledge.  Power is easy. It is everywhere, as long as you take off the blindfold of morality. Power does not bring corruption, but freedom. Only with power - true power - can we rise to the heights that we deserve to reach. But knowledge, that is a harder path. That journey starts here, in the books of the library.   First, build a THRONE, a place to sit in cold detachment. Then construct an unbreakable PHILOSOPHY, one that describes you. On that structure weave SORCERY, the light that guides. Only then, finally, can you CONQUER all.

title: A Transport Network
text: A warning, if you wish to restore the portals here.  Don't.  But I know it won't stop you. History is made by those who disregard warnings. The portals are blocked, sealed on the other side. There are a number, strewn across the Reach. Find them and unclog them to return here. The magic of the Dreaming Stone will do the rest. For my conscience, at least prepare for what follows. There will be blood, a shattering of dreams, and the burning stare of the sun. Consider yourself twice-warned.

title: Rasmodel’s Diary
text: Oh, how this wretched thing has brought calamity to this sacred place. We were founded on the glorious tenets of Zamorak, not the whispering of some crystal stolen from the desert. Yet, look how they bandy around it, as though it were the most marvellous thing. I will not have it. Vulketra and his deranged fanatics need this stone for their schemes; need its power to turn against my forces. They need its strength to bind the demons to their wills and slaughter me and mine. I shall not give them the satisfaction. The stone will be destroyed. I will see to it. I am done with its whispering and the madness it inspires in my once glorious fraternity. It shall fall to the edge of my blade and I will see it shatter to dust. I will laugh as they mourn its end.

title: Alric's Journal
text: Is it regret or hubris that banishes my dreams each night? I cannot remember the last time I dreamed a dream of my own, and not that of… the other. Perhaps it is the foolishness of an old man, clinging to the sharpness of his youth. The passage of time curses me with a dullness that is not my own. My flesh feels alien to me, as if I am a skin worn by something else. My insides writhe and burn like snakes of fire. Even touch feels strange to me, as if there were layers of strange cloth between me and the world. Is this age? Foolishness? Or something worse? Our demons have said nothing for some time. The voices tell me to ignore it, that I am overthinking things and just need to try to sleep. Yet the others whisper threats and curses from the corners of the room, the cracks in the ceiling, wishing me naught but harm. I have made this place better, stronger, more powerful. It was by my hand that we brought the demons through. They should bow in adoration of my power, yet they laugh at me from behind the curtains and pretend they’re not really there. All will come to respect me. All will come to despise me. The whispers are wrong: I am not mad. The whispers are right.

title: Quartermaster's Journal
text: Am I the only one that works around here? Because it seems like I am. Each day, I log the incoming supplies and assign where they’ll go in the keep; and each day, everyone forgets that I need money to secure them. Instead, they bicker and fight among themselves like pups. We were great once, weren’t we? The mighty Children of Shadows, reborn as Zamorak’s knights of black! We were magi with the power to call a legion of demons to serve at our command. Now, I have to explain to the cook why we’ve got three cabbages between us, and find a way to make it last a week. I would leave, if the Shadows would let me. But they tell me I have work to do, and must stay here to keep it going. I try to ignore them as best I can, but they can be so very cruel.

title: The Gospel of Zamorak
text: Deny what is written. Dispute that you denied it.  Sympathise with the confused. Slit them as they leave. Mourn their death. Blame their brethren. Make a deal with the accused. Take what is offered. Give nothing back. Deny what is written. Repeto -
